title: Which dots belong together?
hook: Four dots, two arrangements. What changes when their gaps swap?

knows: four dots can form a rectangle
doesNotKnow: distance between marks can be a cue for perceptual grouping

misconception: The same unconnected marks must be grouped in one fixed way regardless of their arrangement.
objective: Compare two arrangements of four equal dots and explain that proximity can suggest different visual groupings without guaranteeing how each individual perceives them.

claims.text: Case A has four equal dots with a horizontal center-to-center gap of 40 units and a vertical gap of 88 units; side-by-side neighbors are closer.
claims.source: Demo.tsx defines Case A as across 40 and down 88, then uses half-gaps symmetrically to place four equal-radius circles; 40 < 88. Statement is about this constructed stage.

claims.text: Case B swaps the gaps, 88 units across and 40 units down, so vertically adjacent neighbors are closer. Both cases remain displayed when the view is reset.
claims.source: Demo.tsx Case B coordinates are across 88, down 40; 40 < 88. The seen array retains each selected case while Reset view clears only focus.

claims.text: Closeness is one cue people can use to group what they see; the same dots in another arrangement can suggest a different grouping, although personal perception may differ.
claims.source: OpenStax Psychology 2e, section 5.6, Gestalt Principles of Perception: https://openstax.org/books/psychology-2e/pages/5-6-gestalt-principles-of-perception . Source has not been independently checked for this claim and its limitations.

claims.text: The displayed dots are not joined by connecting lines.
claims.source: Demo.tsx Diagram draws circles without connection lines; both arrangements are authored illustrations, not experimental results.

claims.text: In the recall arrangement the horizontal gap of 6 units is shorter than the vertical gap of 15 units, so side-by-side neighbors are closest; perceived grouping is not guaranteed.
claims.source: The recall specifies horizontal separation 6 and vertical separation 15; 6 < 15. The perception qualification is supported by claim c3 and needs independent checking.

recall.question: Four dots form a rectangle with a 6-unit horizontal gap and a 15-unit vertical gap. Which neighbors are closest?
recall.why: Six is less than fifteen, so side-by-side dots are closer. Proximity can suggest a grouping, though it does not dictate anyone's perception.

meaningfulDifference: Examines spatial grouping from distances rather than how surrounding illumination affects perceived lightness.
